subject: Engineering Mathematics I
title: Integral Calculus — One-Mark MCQ Practice
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit III scope; not official university questions or PYQs.

questions.q: The antiderivative of a function f(x) is also called its:
questions.explanation: An indefinite integral represents the family of all antiderivatives of a function.

questions.q: The constant of integration in an indefinite integral is usually denoted by:
questions.explanation: Since differentiation removes constants, an arbitrary constant C is added to an indefinite integral.

questions.q: ∫ x^n dx, for n ≠ −1, equals:
questions.explanation: This is the power rule for integration, valid when n is not −1.

questions.q: The integral ∫ dx/x is:
questions.explanation: The logarithmic integral rule gives ∫(1/x)dx = ln|x|+C.

questions.q: ∫ e^x dx is equal to:
questions.explanation: The exponential function e^x is its own derivative and therefore its own antiderivative.

questions.q: The method used to integrate a product of two functions is commonly called:
questions.explanation: Integration by parts follows from the product rule of differentiation.

questions.q: The formula for integration by parts is:
questions.explanation: The standard integration-by-parts formula is ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du.

questions.q: The substitution method of integration is based primarily on the:
questions.explanation: Integration by substitution reverses the chain rule of differentiation.

questions.q: The definite integral ∫_a^b f(x)dx represents a signed:
questions.explanation: A definite integral can represent signed area between a curve and the x-axis over an interval.

questions.q: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, if F'(x)=f(x), then ∫_a^b f(x)dx equals:
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem evaluates a definite integral using an antiderivative at the limits.

questions.q: If f(x) is continuous on [a,b], then ∫_a^b f(x)dx is:
questions.explanation: Continuity on a closed interval guarantees the existence of the definite integral.

questions.q: The integral of an odd function over [−a,a] is:
questions.explanation: The areas on the two sides of the origin cancel for an odd function over a symmetric interval.

questions.q: The integral of an even function over [−a,a] can be written as:
questions.explanation: For an even function, the two halves of a symmetric interval contribute equally.

questions.q: A double integral over a plane region is commonly used to calculate:
questions.explanation: Double integrals can calculate area and, with an appropriate integrand, volume, mass and other quantities.

questions.q: In a double integral ∬_R 1 dA, the value represents the:
questions.explanation: Integrating 1 over a region gives its area.

questions.q: For a rectangular region R=[a,b]×[c,d], ∬_R f(x,y)dA can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: A rectangular region permits an iterated integral with constant limits in both variables.

questions.q: Changing the order of integration in a double integral requires primarily a change in the:
options: Description of the region and limits
questions.answer: Description of the region and limits
questions.explanation: The same region must be described correctly using the reversed order, with corresponding limits changed.

questions.q: The Jacobian for the transformation x=r cosθ, y=r sinθ is:
questions.explanation: For polar coordinates, dxdy = r drdθ, so the Jacobian magnitude is r.

questions.q: In polar coordinates, x²+y² is equal to:
questions.explanation: Since x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ, x²+y²=r².

questions.q: The differential area element in polar coordinates is:
questions.explanation: The polar-coordinate area element contains the Jacobian factor r.

questions.q: A triple integral is naturally used to integrate over a:
questions.explanation: Triple integrals extend double integration to three-dimensional regions.

questions.q: The volume of a solid region V can be represented by:
questions.explanation: Integrating 1 throughout a three-dimensional region gives its volume.

questions.q: In cylindrical coordinates, the Cartesian variables x and y are expressed as:
questions.explanation: Cylindrical coordinates use polar coordinates in the xy-plane together with z.

questions.q: The cylindrical-coordinate volume element is:
questions.explanation: The Jacobian for cylindrical coordinates is r.

questions.q: Which coordinate system is particularly suitable for a sphere centered at the origin?
questions.explanation: Spherical coordinates naturally describe spherical surfaces using constant radial distance.

questions.q: The volume element in spherical coordinates contains the factor:
questions.explanation: For the conventional spherical coordinates, dV=ρ²sinφ dρ dφ dθ.

questions.q: If density is variable over a solid, the mass is obtained using:
questions.explanation: Mass is the volume integral of density over the solid.

questions.q: The average value of f(x,y) over a region R of area A is:
questions.explanation: The average value is the integral divided by the area of the region.

questions.q: When converting a double integral from Cartesian to polar coordinates, the integrand must be accompanied by:
questions.explanation: The area element changes from dxdy to r drdθ, so the factor r is essential.

questions.q: For a region bounded by x²+y²≤a², polar coordinates give the radial limit as:
questions.explanation: The circle x²+y²=a² becomes r²=a², hence 0≤r≤a for the disk.
